r4_status.H-1: OPEN: case bytes are sourced from the committed tree, but the design records caseTree and then archives HEAD rather than that pinned object, leaving a resolve/copy race if HEAD changes between the two operations.
r4_status.H-2: OPEN: configTree now detects content differences and prevents cross-tree verdict comparison, but compare.py is still directed to load eligibility and proposal data from the current configuration pathname rather than the recorded blob; an in-place committed edit can therefore reinterpret archived runs.

findings.claim: Pinned caseTree/configTree values do not control the bytes subsequently consumed. The design archives the case from HEAD and directs comparison to load case/configuration JSON from current paths, so a concurrent or later same-version commit can make provisioning or eligibility use bytes different from the recorded objects.
findings.evidence: metasystem/plans/benchmark-case-configuration-design.md:50-58 records caseTree but specifies `git archive HEAD:benchmark/cases/<id>/<v>`; metasystem/plans/benchmark-case-configuration-design.md:71-73 records configTree; metasystem/plans/benchmark-case-configuration-design.md:198-202 directs compare.py to current case/configuration paths. Current eligibility is pathname-based at benchmark/compare.py:533-544.
findings.fix: Resolve one source commit first, derive both object IDs from it, archive/read the case and configuration by those exact objects, and make compare load eligibility/proposal semantics from recorded caseTree/configTree or the recorded measuring commit. Add fixtures where HEAD advances or a same-version file is committed after the cohort.

findings.claim: The schema-v1 resume adapter is incomplete for cohorts that have not yet provisioned every repetition. Legacy state records only specId, not mission id or contract path; after specs/ is deleted, resolving the alias to the canonical pair would provision a new target with mission id taskrun, while the resumed legacy path expects mission id bm-* and mission-bm-*.contract.md.
findings.evidence: metasystem/plans/benchmark-case-configuration-design.md:179-189 promises resume in every phase and says mission id and contract path are already recorded; benchmark/run-cohort.sh:220-230 shows schema-v1 state records neither; benchmark/run-cohort.sh:265-277 derives the legacy mission id/path from specId and calls prepare_repetition for phase `new`; metasystem/plans/benchmark-case-configuration-design.md:190 assigns taskrun to new runs and :233-241 treats mission id/path changes as normal pair-provisioning differences.
findings.fix: Specify a legacy-resume provisioning mode for every unstarted repetition that preserves the alias mission id, contract filename and runner paths while sourcing committed canonical case/configuration bytes. Fixture schema-v1 states in `new`, `awaiting-approval`, `running`, and post-grading advancement after specs/ deletion.

findings.claim: The documentation plan omits the promised cross-machine legacy-resume procedure and the rule for reading historical case/configuration objects. Schemas and ordinary authoring examples do not tell another machine how to locate pinned bytes or resume schema-v1 states after specs/ is removed.
findings.evidence: metasystem/plans/benchmark-case-configuration-design.md:181-189 promises cross-machine resume; metasystem/plans/benchmark-case-configuration-design.md:246-267 lists README content and procedures but includes neither legacy resume nor historical object lookup.
findings.fix: Document schema-v1 resume, alias-preserving provisioning, and retrieval/validation of caseTree/configTree bytes, including commands and failure behavior when the recorded Git objects are unavailable.

summary: Four round-4 issues are closed: independenceReason is projected, equivalence uses one difference list, versions are bounded, and acceptance no longer asks for an embedded immutability digest. The central pinning work is not fully closed: recorded object IDs are not consistently used as the source of bytes, and current-path eligibility can reinterpret archived evidence. The legacy resume promise also fails for unprovisioned repetitions because schema-v1 state does not record the claimed mission/path facts and canonical alias provisioning changes them. Projection and compatibility otherwise cover the six shipped aliases; mission id taskrun has no present grammar, fence-key, filename, or runner-path collision; raw-byte instrument integrity avoids formatting and line-ending ambiguity; and refusing every unpinned cohort case/configuration version is the safe CLI rule.
